source_span: "Inverse heating oil is still the 10-year... Trading as if they were the same asset. if we want relief on rates we first need relief on energy."
source_chain: Middle East/Russian refinery capacity is damaged and the US struck Iranian tankers during market hours while oil was already rising, therefore diesel/gasoil/heating oil/TTF gas broke out past their 2022 highs and dragged the 10-year to 4.80% (Amanda Ross runs inverse heating oil vs. the 10-year as the same trade), therefore rates cannot get relief until energy does first -- invalidated only if the energy driver reverses (George Cole's test: fundamental not fragile as long as rates vol hasn't broken higher; forecasts show 10yr 30-40bp lower 'if the driver goes away').
pulse_chain: Refinery damage across the Middle East/Russia breaks out diesel, gasoil, heating oil and European gas (TTF at a post-2023 high, above 2022 levels), pushing the 10-year to 4.80%, therefore Goldman's desk states rates cannot rally until energy falls first (Amanda Ross's inverse-heating-oil-vs-10-year trade), therefore watch energy not the Fed -- invalidated only if the energy driver reverses (George Cole: fundamental not fragile since rates vol hasn't broken higher; GS forecasts 10yr 30-40bp lower if the driver goes away).
why: The pulse keeps the same bank (Goldman), the same named trade and trader, the same 'energy must fall before rates can rally' mechanism, and the same invalidation (George Cole's rates-vol test / driver reversing 30-40bp), with the Waller/hike-odds paragraph added as a one-session exception rather than a reversal of any step.
